title: Are Never-Trumpers Welcome in the Democratic Party? Mehdi Asks Sarah Longwell
author: Mehdi Hasan
content:
The 2024 election was a disaster for Democrats. And with midterms around the
corner and the 2028 presidential election looming ahead, the Democratic Party
has a lot of work to do.

But what, exactly, went wrong in 2024? And will the Democrats be able to
successfully sway not just independents, but former Trump voters?

[Subscribe now](https://zeteo.com/subscribe)

To get to the bottom of these questions, The Bulwark co-founder **Sarah
Longwell** has conducted hundreds of focus groups across the United States and
now provides key insights from those sessions in her best-selling new book,
_[How to Eat An Elephant: One Voter at a
Time](https://bookshop.org/p/books/how-to-eat-an-elephant-one-voter-at-a-time-
sarah-longwell/6a0996cb43d2ef5b?ean=9781250464170)_.

Reflecting on the failure of the Harris campaign in 2024, she tells Mehdi, **"
People who were more centrist thought she was too progressive, and people who
were more progressive thought she was too centrist. She was ill-defined and
she didn't come out and define herself."**

[Share](https://zeteo.com/p/are-never-trumpers-welcome-in-
the?utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&action=share)

But as a former Republican operative turned Never-Trumper, how much weight
should the Democratic Party put into Longwell's strategic advice? In this
interview, Mehdi presents much of the left's criticisms to Longwell and
presses her on:

  * If she and other former Republicans want to push the Democratic Party to the right

  * Whether Kamala Harris listened too much to The Bulwark and its centrist messaging during her 2024 campaign

  * Why she believes Liz Cheney campaigning with Kamala Harris is defensible while Democratic candidates campaigning with Hasan Piker isn't

  * Whether she understands why some on the left are suspicious of her and Never-Trump colleagues

  * If she agrees that the Republican Party she was previously a part of played a role in creating Trump and MAGA

  * Whether she prefers House Democrats prioritizing the investigation of Trump administration officials or the impeachment of Trump himself if they take control of Congress

  * What it was like working for the notorious right-wing lobbyist nicknamed 'Dr. Evil' and whether she has any regrets.
